subject.title: fix: preserve zero sequence ids in sdk events

question: Should the SDK intentionally change normalized IDs for protocol-valid `seq: 0` or `ts: 0` events now, accepting that consumers may see corrected replay and dedupe keys after upgrade?
rationale: The patch is technically correct and narrowly fixes a protocol mismatch, but normalized IDs are consumer-visible dedupe keys and repository policy requires explicit ownership of intentional compatibility changes.

options.title: Adopt corrected zero-preserving IDs
options.body: Merge the narrow fix and treat the new zero-inclusive key as the canonical SDK identity for these events.

options.title: Keep the existing ID contract
options.body: Do not merge if maintainers consider the previously truncated string format immutable and require a future versioned identity scheme.

recommendation.title: Adopt corrected zero-preserving IDs
recommendation.body: Merge the narrow fix and treat the new zero-inclusive key as the canonical SDK identity for these events.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail is the commit that introduced and merged the SDK package and its event contract.
